A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Finding Dori study. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite changes in title, organization and numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Stable Diffusion experiments on pruning vulnerabilities, memorization locality and adversarial fine-tuning, with quantitative and qualitative appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds unlearning comparisons, broader activation analyses and further robustness and unintended-memorization tests.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same embedding optimization and adversarial fine-tuning procedure, including alternating initialization, surrogate images and the combined mitigation and utility losses. LoRA is tested as an alternative configuration without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use LAION memorized and non-memorized images and COCO for the same image-replication and generation-quality tasks. The additions concern comparison methods, model configurations and analyses of retained data rather than new dataset or domain coverage.

E2.justification: v2 retains NeMo and Wanda and adds evaluated mitigation comparators ESD, Concept Ablation and SISS in Tables 2–3. It also evaluates UnlearnDiffAtk implemented with GCG as an alternative attack in Appendices G.1 and I.6; v1 only cited the UnlearnDiffAtk paper.

E3.justification: v2 adds Memorization Rate (MR), the fraction of images exceeding SSCD 0.7 in any of ten generations. New experiments introduce per-image SISS with 35 updates, ESD/Concept Ablation with 10,000/12,000 updates, rank-128 LoRA configurations and a 1,000-image fine-tuning-data check. The original default Dori and COCO evaluation settings remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained sensitivity and loss-ablation studies, v2 adds activation analysis across self-attention, cross-attention and convolutional layers (Appendix J.3), unsuccessful LoRA variants, testing against UnlearnDiffAtk and a check for newly induced memorization (Appendices I.5–I.7). These address additional mechanism, robustness and side-effect questions.

E5.justification: Existing ± reporting, activation error bars, generation/optimization seed variation and five-seed sampling for the ten-prompt Wanda experiment are retained. No changed repeated-run count or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial baseline and MR results: Table 2 reports attacked MR values of 0.98 for ESD, 0.97 for Concept Ablation, 0.39 for SISS and 0.02 for the proposed mitigation. Existing Wanda template results also change: prompt-initialized, 50-step SSCDOrig rises from 0.10±0.06 in v1 Table 2 to 0.51±0.11 in v2 Table 4. The proposed method's headline SSCD and FID values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 introduces MR's aggregation definition, the formal SISS objective in Appendix E.2 and a runtime expression in Appendix I.5. The Dori update, fine-tuning losses and locality equations are otherwise retained. No new locality theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central pruning-vulnerability, nonlocality and robust-mitigation contributions remain. However, v2's conclusion asserts that effective removal requires global model interventions, strengthening v1's tentative suggestion that interventions affecting all weights may be necessary.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands explanations distinguishing individual-image memorization from concept unlearning and interpreting baseline and LoRA failures. It adds explicit single-model generalizability and adversary-access limitations, discusses embeddings' relationship to natural prompts, and qualifies fine-tuning success with a residual highly duplicated sample.

D1.justification: v2 adds baseline implementation settings, LoRA configurations, target-count disclosure and runtime estimates. However, v1 Section 5.2's explicit fine-tuning settings—Adam at 1e-5, batch size 4 and 25 surrogate images per prompt—are omitted rather than relocated. Hardware, software and existing data-access disclosures largely remain.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against concept and data unlearning, adding discussion and citations for SISS, ESD, Concept Ablation, defensive unlearning, LoRA and GCG. The previously cited UnlearnDiffAtk work now receives a substantive comparison explaining Dori's claimed distinct role.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and central narrative are extensively rewritten. v1's standalone fine-tuning Section 5 becomes v2 Section 4.4, activation and weight analyses receive separate subsections, diffusion-training background moves to Appendix E, and the contents pages are removed. Reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 3 is split into v2 Figures 3–4, mitigation results are redistributed into new comparison tables, and MR columns expand tables throughout. v2 adds surrogate-image examples and the broader layer-analysis figure, alongside changed headers, typography and float placement. The existing qualitative image grids are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's pruning-focused evaluation, v2 adds meaningful unlearning comparisons, broader layer tests and checks for unintended memorization. MR also exposes residual failures obscured by summary scores. These gains are tempered by the omission of essential fine-tuning hyperparameters and stronger claims that global updates are necessary, which the finite empirical tests do not establish.
